known.title: Follow-up: Run shared-input checks for documentation-only changes

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - adoption guidance is edited in a later release.
The named proof checks isolated phrases, so it would still pass if the guidance said not to add the checks to the settings. It also reads the worker brief template directly: moving the paragraph below the prototype marker would pass this test even though `src/forge/worker.py:665-669` removes it from the delivered brief. The proof therefore does not guard the affirmative settings instruction at both delivery boundaries.
findings.title: Gate: test_1_adoption_review_keeps_shared_input_checks

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 2
Case: normal use - an adopted content app loads Markdown records through a glob, and a pull request changes one record without naming it in code. For apps using Forge's generated tests check, the docs-only classifier can skip both the recommended Python `always_test` entries and TypeScript `fast_test` commands. `src/forge/docskip.py:111-116` searches for the changed basename, and `src/forge/templates/review-tests.py:102-105` skips the tests unless the repository has a required-tests list. The invalid input can therefore reach the full run after merge. The Python brief names that list at `src/forge/templates/brief.md:382-385`, but the adoption guidance does not connect it to these checks.
Adds work: cover documentation-only shared inputs; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
